title: Copilot Studio: agent node runs an AI agent as a workflow step
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, maker settings, credit controls and API requests are supported by the sources checked. Its statements about undocumented node-specific controls and pricing are appropriately narrow.

claims.where: front matter: products
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365) and Microsoft Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365)", "Microsoft Copilot Studio"]

claims.where: front matter: status; What's changing
claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing
claims.claim: The roadmap target date is September CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "September CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: previewDate; What's changing
claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is April CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "April CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: releasePhase; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap lists both General Availability and Preview.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: Web is the only listed platform.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: An agent node lets an AI agent reason over a workflow step.
claims.quote: The agent node lets a flow hand a step over to an AI agent that can reason, call tools, and pull from knowledge sources before returning a result.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The agent can call tools during the workflow step.
claims.quote: Equip the agent with tools (Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and connectors) so it can take action.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The agent can use SharePoint and public websites as knowledge sources.
claims.quote: Ground the agent in knowledge (SharePoint sites, public websites) so it can answer from your content.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The agent result becomes dynamic content for later workflow steps.
claims.quote: The agent response then becomes available as dynamic content that you can use in any subsequent step.

claims.where: What's changing: adding the node; Scope
claims.claim: Makers open Workflows, open or create a workflow, use Build for an existing workflow, and select Agent on the Add panel.
claims.quote:
In Copilot Studio, go to **Workflows** and open an existing workflow, or create a new one.
Existing workflow: Open the workflow and go to the **Build** tab.
Select the **Agent** icon on the Add panel.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: An existing agent is selected from published agents.
claims.quote: **An existing agent**: Select a published agent from a list.

claims.where: What's changing: existing agent
claims.claim: An existing agent runs with its already configured instructions, tools and knowledge.
claims.quote: The agent runs with whatever instructions, tools, and knowledge it was already configured with.

claims.where: What's changing: New agent for this workflow
claims.claim: A new inline agent's instructions, tools, knowledge and output shape are configured in the node and travel with the workflow.
claims.quote: The agent's instructions, tools, knowledge, and output shape are configured in the node itself and travel with the workflow.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: An inline agent is scoped to its workflow and cannot be reused outside it.
claims.quote:
Can the inline agent be reused outside this workflow?
No. An inline agent is scoped to its workflow.

claims.claim: MCP servers can be attached as tools.
claims.quote: **Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers**: Prebuilt servers that expose a curated set of capabilities.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Any Power Platform connector action can be attached as a tool.
claims.quote: **Connectors**: Any Power Platform connector action.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The agent decides at run time which attached tools to call.
claims.quote: The agent decides at run time which of its attached tools to call, in what order, and with what arguments.

claims.where: What's changing: tool selection

claims.quote: The agent decides at run time which of its attached tools to call, in what order, and with what arguments.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The agent decides the arguments used in tool calls.
claims.quote: The agent decides at run time which of its attached tools to call, in what order, and with what arguments.

claims.quote: Turn on **Work IQ** to let the agent use the running user's recent work activity

claims.claim: The agent waits for the connection owner's reply before continuing.
claims.quote: The agent emails the connection owner for input and waits for a reply before continuing.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Structured output exposes individual agent-written fields to downstream actions.
claims.quote: When you pick a structured output, each field becomes its own dynamic-content token that downstream actions can reference directly.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Attached tools can take actions such as sending messages or calling APIs.
claims.quote: Tools give the agent the ability to *do* actions such as send a message, query a record, run a search, or call an API.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Without tools the agent can only read and reason.
claims.quote: Without tools, the agent can only read and reason. With tools, it can also act.

claims.where: What's changing: release-phase qualification; Open questions
claims.claim: The node's Learn page does not identify which part of the feature remains in preview.
claims.quote: Searched: read the complete https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/workflows-experience/agent-node-workflow for preview qualifications; none identifies the scope of the roadmap's Preview phase.

claims.where: Why it matters: documented publish procedure
claims.claim: The designer's documented publish procedure contains no administrator review step.
claims.quote: Searched: Publish your workflow in https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/workflows-experience/flow-designer; it says to select Publish when there are no errors, with no administrator review step.

claims.where: controls[3].ui and controls[3].api; summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk

claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "agent node" "tenant" "switch"; "agent node" "disable" "workflow"; read agent-node-workflow, flows-overview, manage-usage-github-copilot-harness and admin-data-loss-prevention on Learn. No node-specific disable switch found.

claims.where: Why it matters: who can build in the environment
claims.claim: Existing Copilot Studio and environment permissions control who can create agents.
claims.quote: To control who can create agents, use your existing Copilot Studio and environment permissions.

claims.quote: The harness used to build this agent uses usage-based billing. Using, building, testing, and evaluating agents might consume Copilot Credits.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No rate specific to the agent node is published as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent node" "rate" "credits". Read agent-node-workflow and billing-credit-overview on Learn, plus requirements-messages-management search excerpts. No agent-node-specific rate found; the latter page states its rates concern the standard harness.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Credits are charged to the environment where the workload runs.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged to the environment where the agent runs

claims.where: Cost and licensing: prepaid capacity
claims.claim: Environment consumption can use prepaid capacity.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged to the environment where the agent runs, from prepaid capacity or through the environment's pay-as-you-go billing plan

claims.where: Cost and licensing: pay-as-you-go
claims.claim: Environment consumption can use a linked pay-as-you-go billing plan.
claims.quote: When you link an environment to a pay-as-you-go billing plan, you can bill Copilot Studio usage to the associated Azure subscription.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: not individual makers

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Environment prepaid allocations are managed at Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits.
claims.quote:
In the navigation pane, select **Licensing**.
Under **Products**, select **Copilot Studio**.
Select **Manage Copilot Credits**.
Select the environment.
Enter the number of Copilot Credits to allocate.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Capacity management requires Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or an equivalent role able to manage licensing and capacity.
claims.quote: To manage Copilot Studio capacity, you need the Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Environment capacity controls apply across Copilot Studio workloads, rather than only agent nodes.
claims.quote: The capacity and consumption controls in the Power Platform admin center apply across Copilot Studio. They aren't exclusive to the Microsoft Copilot harness.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Clearing Draw from the available capacity in my tenant prevents drawing unallocated tenant prepaid capacity after the allocation is consumed.
claims.quote: When you clear this option, the environment doesn't draw from unallocated prepaid capacity in the tenant after it consumes its allocation.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Turning off tenant-pool draw does not stop consumption through a linked pay-as-you-go plan.
claims.quote: This setting doesn't prevent consumption through a pay-as-you-go billing plan linked to the environment.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Azure budgets
claims.claim: Azure budgets send notifications but do not stop Copilot Studio consumption.
claims.quote: Azure budgets and alerts send notifications but don't stop Copilot Studio consumption.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Tenant-pool draw is selected by default for eligible Copilot Studio environments without allocation configuration.
claims.quote: For eligible Copilot Studio environments, **Draw from the available capacity in my tenant** is selected by default when no allocation configuration exists.

claims.where: Governance controls: environment group rule
claims.claim: An environment group rule governing tenant draw makes the environment-level setting read-only.
claims.quote: When you publish a rule, it governs every environment in the group. The environment-level setting becomes read-only in the Power Platform admin center

claims.where: Governance controls: environment group rule
claims.claim: Programmatic requests cannot override the group-governed tenant-draw setting.
claims.quote: Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the `TenantPoolLockedByPolicy` error.

go to **Workflows** and open an existing workflow

claims.claim: No central enforcement setting for node human assistance is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "Request human assistance when unsure" "policy"; "agent node" "Request human assistance" API enforce admin disable. Read agent-node-workflow and admin-data-loss-prevention on Learn; no central enforcement setting found.

claims.claim: Evaluations are available only for new agents created in workflows.
claims.quote: Evaluations are only available for new agents created in workflows.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The evaluation limit is 20 evaluations per agent node per day.

claims.claim: The workflow overview says new runs are blocked after environment prepaid capacity is fully consumed until capacity is available.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Running workflows complete normally when prepaid capacity is consumed.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The Workflows page has a Credit usage (last 30 days) column.
claims.quote: The **Credit usage (last 30 days)** column shows the credits that a workflow consumed during the last 30 days.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The node can be tested before publishing using its Test tab.
claims.quote:
Select the agent node to open its property side panel.
Select the **Test** tab.
Enter inputs manually, or use inputs from a previous workflow run.
Select **Run test**.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Evaluate is the node evaluation entry point after a test run.
claims.quote:
Run a test for the agent node.
Select **Evaluate**.
Create a grader or select an existing grader.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Data policies govern Power Platform connector tools in Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from [using Power Platform connectors as tools](advanced-connectors) in Copilot Studio agents, configure a data policy with the connectors you want to block.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks tools in connected MCP servers that rely on them.
claims.quote: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks access to tools in connected MCP servers, which rely on Power Platform connectors for connectivity.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Advanced Connector Policies govern certified connectors.
claims.quote: **Certified connectors** | Supported | First-party and certified third-party connectors. Full allow/block at the connector and action level.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Advanced Connector Policies support blocking entire MCP servers.
claims.quote: Within advanced connector policies, administrators can see MCP servers listed alongside other connector types and can choose to block an entire MCP server.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Custom and HTTP connectors are not supported by ACP and must still be governed with classic data policies.
claims.quote: Custom connectors and HTTP connectors aren't yet supported. They're planned as a separate rule type in the future. For governing custom connectors and HTTP connectors today, continue using classic [data policies](prevent-data-loss).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Connector operations are evaluated against the hosting environment's effective policy.
claims.quote: At runtime, when a connector operation is invoked, it queries the effective policy for the current hosting environment.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: ACP design-time enforcement is rolling out to Copilot Studio.
claims.quote:
Design-time enforcement is rolling out across maker portals in the following order:
1. **Power Automate maker portal**
2. **Copilot Studio**

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: ACP enforcement is runtime-only until design-time support becomes available for the workload.
claims.quote: Until design-time support is available in a given maker portal, ACP operates as a runtime-only enforcement for that workload.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Policy-blocked tools, connectors, AI models and skills appear disabled in Microsoft Copilot harness agent pickers.
claims.quote: When a data policy or Advanced Connector Policy blocks a tool, connector, AI model, or skill, that item appears disabled wherever you'd normally select it, such as the tools list, model list, or skills list.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP has a tenant-level policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: In the initial release, Work IQ MCP provides tenant-level policy control. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, tenant administrators can turn Work IQ MCP policy on or off for the tenant.

claims.where: Governance controls: Work IQ MCP path; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The documented Work IQ MCP path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy, when available.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation, select **Agents** > **Tools**.
In the tools registry, select **Work IQ MCP**.
On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the **Policy** tab when it's available.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP tenant policy can allow or deny specific MCP tool requests.
claims.quote: It adds a request-time governance layer that can allow or deny specific MCP tool requests based on tenant policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not explicitly confirm that Work IQ MCP policy governs the inline agent node's Work IQ option.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent node" "Work IQ" "policy". Read agent-node-workflow and policy-governance-mcp; reviewed add-work-iq search excerpts. General Work IQ MCP governance is documented, but no passage maps the inline-node option to that policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The node page does not identify whose credentials its connector actions or attached SharePoint knowledge use.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent node" "credentials"; Copilot Studio "agent node" "SharePoint" "identity". Read agent-node-workflow and general identity search excerpts; no node-specific connector or SharePoint credential identity was stated.

claims.where: Scope: prerequisites
claims.claim: The node's Learn page names no licence prerequisite for adding the node.
claims.quote: Searched: read the complete https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/workflows-experience/agent-node-workflow for licence prerequisites. It documents usage-based billing but names no licence prerequisite for adding the node.

claims.where: Governance controls: monthly agent limits
claims.claim: Administrators can set individual monthly agent limits from Licensing > Copilot Studio > Manage Agents.
claims.quote:
In the Power Platform admin center, go to **Licensing** > **Copilot Studio**.
Select **Manage Agents**.
Select the agent, and then select **Set limit**.
Enter the monthly Copilot Credit limit.

claims.where: Governance controls: monthly agent limits qualification
claims.claim: Learn does not state that individual agent monthly limits cap agent-node credit consumption inside a workflow.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "agent node" "monthly" "limit". Read node and harness cost pages and manage-copilot-studio-copilot-credits-capacity search excerpts. They document agent limits, but not how those limits cap an agent node inside a workflow.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState
claims.claim: The default state is user-opt-in: a maker chooses to add the node, with no documented node-specific admin enablement switch.
claims.quote:
In Copilot Studio, go to **Workflows** and open an existing workflow, or create a new one.
Select the **Agent** icon on the Add panel. The configuration panel opens for the agent node.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model
claims.claim: The licensing model is consumption.
claims.quote: Agents, workflows, and apps powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness and customer conversations handled by Microsoft Contact Center Intelligence use a usage-based billing structure.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Workflow results can vary between runs when actions use AI.
claims.quote: Results can vary when actions use AI or retrieve changing data.
